newsitem.title: USA: Union seeks support on ADM director liability plan.
newsitem.headline: Union seeks support on ADM director liability plan.

text.p: The United Brotherhood of Carpenters Pension Fund said on Friday that it is seeking support for its proposal to hold Archer Daniels Midland Co directors personally liable in cases of gross negligence.
The union, which holds about 770,000 ADM shares, said it wrote to several hundred major money managers and pension funds that hold ADM stock, urging support for its proposal.
The proposal is among the items to be voted on by shareholders at ADM's annual meeting on October 17.

"We believe that the issue of director personal monetary liability should be viewed in the context of the overall corporate governance policies and practices in place at ADM," the union said. "Like many shareholders, the fund is greatly concerned with the corporate conduct that has prompted a criminal investigation of ADM pricing practies and an increasing amount of civil litigation."

ADM is the focus of a federal antitrust investigation into possible price-fixing in the lysine, citric acid and high-fructose corn syrup. It also faces suits from shareholders and customers stemming from that probe.

In its proxy statement, ADM said it recommends that shareholders vote against the union's proposal, saying the company must provide board members with protection from liability in order to attract qualified candidates.
ADM added that the proposal, if passed, also would make board members easier targets for "non-meritorious lawsuits."

"Determining what does or does not constitute 'gross negligence' involves legal and factual questions that do not lend themselves to simple definition," ADM said. "The uncertain risks of litigation subject directors to considerable risks."
